body:
## Architecture Finding

**Type**: coupling/interface-violation
**Affected area**: `common/variables.go`, `common/logger.go`, `common/identities.go`, `htfs/directory.go`, `settings/settings.go`

Foundational packages use `init()` to inspect CLI arguments, mutate exported process-global flags, start background goroutines, and create product/holotree directories. `htfs` additionally performs directory creation when it is merely imported. Consequently, package import order and test process state become implicit runtime inputs, and the command layer cannot construct an isolated configuration or use these packages safely as reusable libraries.

## Impact

Tests must save and restore global state; embedding RCC or adding commands can trigger I/O and goroutines before configuration is validated; concurrent or multi-profile execution cannot be isolated. The dependency boundary is inverted: domain/storage packages own CLI lifecycle side effects.

## Recommendation

Introduce an explicit runtime/bootstrap object owned by the composition root (`cmd/rcc`). Move argument/environment parsing, directory provisioning, logger lifecycle, and mutable execution flags into that bootstrap/context. Pass narrow dependencies into operations and storage packages; keep package initialization declarative only. Migrate incrementally, starting with filesystem provisioning in `htfs` and common runtime globals.

## October 10 evidence reconciliation

The #226 worker-limit fix is integrated through #227, but import-time initialization remains a separate architecture issue. Current effects include CLI argv/environment inspection and logger/timeline/identity goroutines in common init functions, directory initialization in htfs/directory.go, and settings/environment/proxy initialization in settings/settings.go. There is no root-owned explicit bootstrap/dependency-injection boundary yet; do not infer completion from the CLI worker regression or green artifact tests.

The root-reviewed assessment and raw focused coverage are retained under `work/rcc-swarm/evidence/remaining-triage.md` and `remaining-focus-coverage.log`. This reconciliation adds current disposition evidence; it leaves the issue open and does not promote #185 governance authority.
